newsitem.title: UK: Callebaut sees Europe chocolate price up in autumn.
newsitem.headline: Callebaut sees Europe chocolate price up in autumn.

text.p: Continental Europe's chocolate prices should rise this autumn due to a persistently strong British pound, Klaus Jacobs, chairman of Barry Callebaut AG, said on Tuesday.
Chocolate makers "have to increase prices", he told reporters in London while discussing the company's planned initial public offering in early 1998.

Jacobs said chocolate companies were normally supplied for a year, and sometimes two, so slimmer margins due to the pound's initial strength against other European currencies had mostly been absorbed.

"Chocolate is usually covered for a year, maybe even two years by some people, so you wouldn't see an increase in price automatically," he said. But "the pound is now about six months stronger so, we'll see some (price increases). We know it's going to happen...in the fall.
He said the companies were discussing price increases of 10 or 15 percent, which he felt the market could take.
Overall, cocoa supply and demand was seen mostly in balance.

Asked about a large cocoa position believed to be held by trade house Phibro, Jacobs said the "Phibro position has been taken into consideration. Everybody in the marketplace knows that there is this position. So, you can also say in a way, it has already been discounted, or has been taken care of."
